🇺🇸🇷🇺🇮🇷 Iran's blockade standoff may be frozen in place. The Russia-Ukraine front is not. And Europe is about to make it worse.

Prof. David Gibbs, historian at the University of Arizona and U.S. foreign policy scholar, says the panic setting in across European capitals is driving irrational escalation, and someone is going to miscalculate.

Ukraine struck Kaliningrad for the first time. Russian ships are being hit off the Libyan coast. The wars are starting to merge.

Gibbs is clear: Russia is winning. Its economy is not collapsing. Putin's approval sits above 70%. He has no reason to take the bait. 

But Europe keeps baiting anyway, talking openly about military maneuvers around Kaliningrad, a piece of sovereign Russian territory with tactical nukes on it.

On the Democrats: don't expect them to end the Iran war. In 2006, they had the votes to cut off Iraq funding. Pelosi said no. Same calculation, different war.

On Trump and Putin in Shenzhen: three powers in a room saying they want stability. That's not nothing.

The Iran front may hold. The Russia front is a different story, and the people pushing hardest for escalation have no nukes, no plan, and no memory of how the last century's wars started.

🇺🇸🇮🇷🇷🇺 Trump wants to AVOID ANOTHER WAR with Iran. But the next escalation could happen WITHOUT anyone ordering it.

Brandon Weichert spoke with retired Lt. Col. Anthony Aguilar about a dangerous new phase of the Iran conflict and growing tensions between Russia and NATO.

Iran's threatened blockade-breaking operation has turned into a bizarre game of disappearing ships, questionable tracking signals and real tankers slipping through.

Anthony believes Tehran is deliberately keeping Washington guessing.

And with American warships, drones and missiles operating in the same waters, ONE mistake could restart the fighting.

There's also Netanyahu.

With Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot attempting to form a government by December 6, Anthony fears Netanyahu could seek another confrontation with Iran before losing power.

Brandon, meanwhile, says he's heard Trump privately wants no part of another war and is increasingly frustrated with Netanyahu. He stressed that this account is unverified.

Then we turned to Russia.

Anthony discussed alleged Ukrainian strikes against Russian vessels near Libya and the Baltic, alongside attacks involving Kaliningrad.

He suspects NATO knows more about these operations than it's admitting, although he offered no direct evidence of NATO involvement.

His concern is that Moscow could eventually treat such attacks as a NATO provocation rather than an isolated Ukrainian operation.

And that could turn a regional war into something MUCH bigger.

We also discussed recent American infrastructure disruptions, including an apparent cyber intrusion at an Illinois dam. Neither of us could establish who was responsible.

Anthony's broader argument was that the world's conflicts are becoming increasingly interconnected, while the people making decisions are struggling to control even one of them.

Trump may want to put Iran on hold until next year. The trouble is, wars don't always wait for presidents to make up their minds.

@WeTheBrandon
